profile.name: Nate Erskine-Smith
profile.bio: Liberal MP for Beaches—East York 2015–2026 and federal Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities (Dec 2024–May 2025); a commercial litigation lawyer before politics; resigned from Parliament July 7, 2026 and announced his council run August 18, 2026.

promises.text: Build more homes through gentle density in neighbourhoods, mid-rise housing on avenues, and greater density around major transit hubs, while ensuring growth comes with access to transit, green space and community infrastructure.
Build non-market housing with ambition and at scale, making the most of land owned by the City and other like-minded non-profits.
Bolster RentSafeTO and crack down on slum landlords to protect tenants.
Expand rapid housing, rent supplements, and both temporary and permanent housing solutions to help people off the street.
Speed up streetcars through FastTrackTO’s plan, including signal and switch upgrades.
Make reliable everyday subway service a priority by addressing slow zones, delays, and recurring maintenance problems.
Reduce the fare cap and save regular transit users more.
Get the work started on the new Cherry Street ramp starting next year.
Prioritize a complete and integrated cycling network, expand BikeShare, and improve street safety.
Oppose the expansion of Billy Bishop Airport.
Accelerate renewable energy and expand rooftop solar on homes and schools.
Work with City staff and neighbourhoods to review every major intersection in the ward to identify practical improvements to make our everyday routes safer.
Deliver a human rights approach to rapid housing solutions so that no one needs to sleep in public spaces.

expensesDetailSource.name: Council Expense Routine Disclosure — Constituency Services & Office Expenses
expensesDetailSource.publisher: City Clerk's Office, City of Toronto
expensesDetailSource.note: Figures are the City's routine disclosure of constituency services and office expenses, shown as published, by category, from 2013. This is a separate publication from the annual remuneration reports in expenses.json, with a narrower scope — office spending only, not pay, benefits or staff salaries — and the two are never added together. Amounts shown as personal funds are the member's own money, as the City reports it. Invoice-level documents stay on the City's site; category amounts link to them.
